# `get_camera_16bit`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Report whether the camera pixel format is the two-bytes-per-pixel format.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | A |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xc4c70, GetBytesPerPix @0x11e920 (64-bit build); 32-bit build bytes-per-pixel get switch in the camera class; image-type enum from the camera library debug information |

Params are not read. Returns a boolean that is true when the backend's bytes-per-pixel is 2. The backend maps format 2 to two bytes per pixel and format 3 to one; any other cached format yields 210. Format 2 is 16-bit raw and format 3 gained 8-bit Bayer, so true means 16-bit raw capture is selected. The result is not a hardware capability bit. Note the interplay with set_camera_16bit, whose true selects format 3, after which this returns false. The 32-bit build maps formats the same way (2 to two bytes, 3 to one, otherwise 210) (READ, 32-bit build).

Side effects: Reads the cached pixel format; writes only caller output and thread-local error state.

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 318 | Camera or backend is closed | `device not connected` |
| 210 | Cached format is neither 2 nor 3 | `not supported` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":53,"method":"get_camera_16bit"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_camera_16bit","result":false,"code":0,"id":53}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_camera_16bit","error":"device not connected","code":318,"id":54}
```
